title: Data Handling
description: Class 5 IMO — Data handling: double bar graphs, pie charts, mean, median and mode, and an introduction to probability (impossible, less likely, equally likely, certain).

topics.title: Double Bar Graphs & Pie Charts
topics.concept:
A double bar graph shows two sets of data side by side, so we can compare them — for example, the marks of boys and girls in each subject. The taller bar shows the larger value.

A pie chart shows parts of a whole as slices of a circle; a slice that is half the circle stands for half the data.

examples.problem: What does a double bar graph let us do?
examples.solution: Compare two sets of data side by side.

examples.problem: A pie chart shows half the circle for cricket. What does that mean?
examples.solution: Half of the people chose cricket.

recap: A double bar graph compares two sets of data.
A pie chart shows parts of a whole as slices.

quiz.q: A double bar graph is used to compare ___ ?
quiz.explanation: It compares two sets of data side by side.

quiz.q: In a bar graph, the taller bar shows the ___ value.
quiz.explanation: A taller bar means a larger value.

topics.title: Mean, Median & Mode
topics.concept:
The mean (average) is the sum of the values divided by how many there are. The median is the middle value when the data is arranged in order. The mode is the value that appears most often.

For 2, 4, 6: mean = (2 + 4 + 6) ÷ 3 = 4. For 3, 5, 7: the median is 5.

examples.solution: 3 appears most often, so the mode is 3.

recap: Median = middle value (in order); mode = most frequent value.

quiz.explanation: 2 appears most often, so the mode is 2.

topics.title: Probability
topics.concept:
Probability describes how likely something is. An event can be certain (sure to happen), impossible (cannot happen), equally likely (a 50-50 chance), or less likely (unlikely).

Getting heads or tails on a fair coin is equally likely. The sun rising tomorrow is certain. Rolling a 7 on a normal six-sided dice is impossible.

examples.problem: How likely is getting heads or tails on a fair coin?
How likely is the sun rising tomorrow?
examples.solution: Certain — it is sure to happen.

recap: Probability words: certain, impossible, equally likely, less likely.
A fair coin gives heads or tails as equally likely.

quiz.q: Rolling a 7 on a normal six-sided dice is ___ ?
quiz.explanation: A normal dice only has 1 to 6, so a 7 is impossible.

quiz.q: A pie chart shows parts of a ___ ?
quiz.explanation: A pie chart shows parts of a whole.

questions.q: Which word describes the value that appears most often?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value.

questions.q: Getting heads when you toss a fair coin is ___ to getting tails.
questions.explanation: Heads and tails are equally likely on a fair coin.

questions.q: Rolling an 8 on a normal six-sided dice is ___ ?
questions.explanation: A dice only shows 1 to 6, so an 8 is impossible.

questions.q: The sun setting in the evening is ___ ?
questions.explanation: The sun setting is certain — it is sure to happen.
3 appears three times, more than any other value.

questions.q: Test scores are 8, 9, 8, 10, 8. What is the mode?
questions.explanation: 8 appears three times, so the mode is 8.

questions.q: A double bar graph is most useful for comparing ___ ?
questions.explanation: It compares two groups side by side.

questions.q: In a class survey, cricket fills half the pie chart. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: Half the circle means half the class chose cricket.
In order, the middle value of five numbers is the third, which is 4.
